Rotation Scoreboard

Every tracked ratio ranked by how stretched its leadership is
How to read it. Every number here is computed on a ratio, not on price.
  • Stretch is the mean of three normalized legs: weekly RSI distance from 50, the z-score of the log-ratio residual vs its 5-year regression channel, and the normalized distance from the 40-week MA. Above +1 means leadership is extended and at risk of rotating out; below −1 means it is washed out and is a candidate to rotate in.
  • State comes from position vs the 40-week MA and the sign of the 13-week ROC. Above MA + rising = Leading (Extended if stretched); above MA + falling = Weakening; below MA + rising = Improving; below MA + falling = Lagging (Washed Out if stretched).
  • Stretch is the warning, ROC is the trigger. An Extended reading says the trade is late, not that it is over. The flip is confirmed when the 13-week ROC crosses below zero or the ratio closes under its 40-week MA.
  • R² is the quality of the 5-year relative-strength trend fit. A low R² means the channel — and so the channel z — is describing noise; lean on the RSI and MA legs instead for those.
